title: Revit Pre-Issue Style QA Review
purpose: Perform repeatable pre-issue style checks for Revit views and sheets covering graphics, view/sheet consistency, annotation, metadata, and print legibility without conflating style QA with technical coordination or formal acceptance.

applies_to.scope: Views and sheets intended for formal issue or major internal review

preconditions: The applicable view, sheet, naming, parameter, and titleblock standards are available.
The issue/review scope has been identified.
Technical coordination and formal acceptance remain governed separately by S5/S7.

steps.name: Check issue-view graphics
actions: Confirm the governed View Template is applied to every issue view.
Check for unintended temporary or local graphics overrides.
Verify lineweights, patterns, halftones, category visibility, linked-model visibility, datum heads, crops, and material/hatch display at representative print scales.
Use detail lines, filled regions, masking regions, and imported/custom patterns only where allowed by their governing instruction.
validation: Issue views display consistently with the applicable governed templates and remain legible at issue scale.
Ad-hoc graphics overrides are absent or explicitly governed.
failure_modes: Temporary view state or local overrides remain in an issue view.
Graphics become illegible or misleading at the intended output scale.

steps.name: Check sheet and view consistency
actions: Confirm approved titleblocks are used and required project/sheet metadata is populated.
Check sheet number/name uniqueness and conformance to the governed naming source.
Check view naming, references, callouts, placement, margins, legends, schedules, north arrows, and scale indicators where required.
Verify revision schedules, clouds, and tags correspond to the current issue state.
validation: Sheets and placed views are internally consistent and reference the governed naming/titleblock structures.
No duplicate sheet number or unresolved orphaned callout is present in the reviewed scope.
failure_modes: A sheet uses a non-governed titleblock or incomplete metadata.
Duplicate or inconsistent sheet/view identity exists.
Issue/revision graphics do not match the intended issue state.

steps.name: Check annotation and notation
actions: Use approved text, tag, symbol, leader, arrowhead, unit, and notation styles.
Run spelling review on issue sheets and verify project abbreviations/technical terms against the applicable governed glossary where one exists.
Confirm tags are driven by governed parameters rather than exploded or disconnected drafting substitutes.
validation: Annotation is legible, consistent, and connected to governed data where applicable.
No unsupported manual style override is used in the reviewed scope.
failure_modes: Unapproved text/tag styles or disconnected drafting substitutes are used.
Units or symbols render incorrectly in the intended output.

steps.name: Record pre-issue QA evidence
actions: Record the reviewed sheets/views and observed deviations.
Correct style defects before issue or route unresolved deviations through the governed exception path.
Retain representative test output where print/PDF appearance is part of the check.
validation: The review scope and unresolved findings are traceable.
A style QA result is not represented as technical coordination sign-off or formal acceptance.
failure_modes: A style review is used as evidence of coordination closure or contractual acceptance.

outputs: Corrected Revit views/sheets or logged deviations
governance_notes: This source is explicitly draft and style-focused; it does not establish technical coordination approval, exchange acceptance, or contractual reliance.
Source example scales, roles, and glossary references remain project/source context unless separately governed.
QA evidence is consumed by higher-level readiness/acceptance gates; it does not create those gates.

provenance.source_title: Revit Style Guide - QA / Review Checklists
provenance.migration_note: Draft L6 style QA source migrated conservatively. Technical coordination and formal acceptance boundaries remain with S5/S7.
